==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|circuler}}, {{m|enm|circuleer}}, {{m|enm|circulere}}, from {{der|en|fro|circulier}} ({{cog|fr|circulaire}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|circularis}}, from {{der|en|la|circulus}}, diminutive of {{m|la|circus|t=ring}}. {{surf|en|circle|-ar|id2=adjective}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|sûr'''′'''kyələr}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈsɜː.kjə.lə/|a=RP,AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈsɜɹ.kjə.ləɹ/|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-circular.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈsɪɾ.kjə.ləɾ/|a=ScE}}
* {{hyph|en|cir|cu|lar}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Of or relating to a [[circle]].
# In the [[shape]] of, or [[moving]] in, a circle.
#: {{syn|en|annular|ring-shaped|O-shaped}}
#: {{cot|en|semicircular|hemicircular<qq:half a circle>|;|egg-shaped|ovoid<qq:ball-like solid>}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|oval|;|round|;|toroid<id:Q12510>|ringlike|round-like}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=5|passage=Here, in the transept and choir, where the service was being held, one was conscious every moment of an increasing brightness; colours glowing vividly beneath the '''circular''' chandeliers, and the rows of small lights on the choristers' desks flashed and sparkled in front of the boys' faces, deep linen collars, and red neckbands.}}
# [[circuitous|Circuitous]] or [[roundabout]].
# Referring back to itself, so as to prevent computation or comprehension; [[infinitely]] [[recursive]].
#: {{co|en|'''circular''' reasoning}}
#: {{ux|en|Your dictionary defines "brave" as "courageous", and "courageous" as "brave". That's a '''circular''' definition.}}
#: ''a '''circular''' formula in a spreadsheet''
# [[distribute|Distributed]] to a large number of persons.
#* {{RQ:Hallam England|passage=a proclamation of Henry III., {{...}} doubtless '''circular''' throughout England}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Perfect; complete.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1632|author=Philip Massinger|title=Maid of Honour|section=act I, scene 2
|passage=A man so absolute and '''circular''' / In all those wished-for rarities that may take / A virgin captive.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} Adhering to a fixed [[circle]] of [[legend]]s; [[cyclic]]; hence, [[mean]]; [[inferior]].
#* '''February 1, 1711''', {{w|John Dennis (dramatist)|John Dennis}}, ''on the Genius and Writings of Shakespeare''
